# /record

The voice half of the story fork, step 3 of the daily loop, F4. A person
records a spoken story about their drawing, hears it back, and can
re-record before committing. On a browser that supports it, this is a real
microphone capture and a real upload, not a stub.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/record` |
| Router file | `app/record.tsx` |
| Flows | F4 Daily create and submit |
| Position in flow | step 3 of 5, the voice half of the type-or-record fork |
| Data calls | one write, `POST /audio`, fired on "Use this recording" |
| Shared surface | none; its own capture/playback UI, not shared with any other screen |

F4 per the inventory. F2's recorded branch also reaches this screen via `app/onboarding/story-select.tsx:60`, which the inventory does not record; see the [F2 flow page](/prototype/workflows/f2-first-run-onboarding).

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## The capture

Go back and type your story instead.', and a disabled pink 'Use this recording' button"></a><figcaption>Open the tile. From <code>npm run capture:board</code> at scribl-app <code>72c3ab8</code>, captured 2026-08-31.</figcaption></figure>

This is the screen's real interface, but it is showing its unsupported-
browser branch, not the microphone UI. The capture tool's headless browser
does not satisfy `isRecordingSupported()` (`src/services/audioRecorder.ts:55-59`,
checked at `app/record.tsx:62`), so the `supported` flag is false and the
screen renders the "Voice notes aren't available here yet" message
(`app/record.tsx:264-266`) instead of the mic button, status text, and
countdown that a real browser with `getUserMedia` and `MediaRecorder` would
show. This is a fact about the capture environment, not about `/record`
being broken -- flagged here rather than describing a mic button that is
not on this tile.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| Detect mic support (`getUserMedia` + `MediaRecorder`) before offering to record | `src/services/audioRecorder.ts:55-59`, checked at `app/record.tsx:62` |
| Start/stop capture with a hard cap at `VOICE_MAX_SECONDS` (30s), visible countdown, auto-stop at zero | `app/record.tsx:112-124`, `:126-146`; countdown UI at `:238-242` |
| Play the take back, or stop mid-playback, with visible playing state (web only) | `app/record.tsx:153-175`, `:246-250` |
| Re-record, discarding the previous take and any already-uploaded ref for it | `app/record.tsx:126-131`, `:252-259` |
| Upload the take via `POST /audio` and carry the returned `audioRef` forward | `app/record.tsx:177-200` |
| Route to `/choose-channels` (default) or `/onboarding/walls`, via a whitelisted `next` param | `app/record.tsx:23-37` |
| Release the mic on unmount, even mid-capture | `app/record.tsx:83` |
| Show an explicit error and refuse to advance on a failed upload | `app/record.tsx:193-199` |

## Data calls

**One write, on "Use this recording."**

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `uploadAudio()` | `POST /audio` | `backend/lambda/handlers/audio-upload.ts` |

The call site is `app/record.tsx:182-186`, calling
`src/services/audioUpload.ts:65-119`. On success it writes `audioRef`,
`audioMime`, and `audioDurationMs` into `useDraftStore` via `setAudio()`
(`app/record.tsx:187-191`), which also clears any typed caption
(`src/stores/useDraftStore.ts:74`), then pushes to the resolved `next` route
(`app/record.tsx:192`). On failure it clears the draft's audio fields and
shows the error inline; it never advances (`app/record.tsx:193-199`).

This screen does not call `dataClient.submit()`. The recording is staged
here; the actual submission happens later, in `/choose-channels`, the same
as the typed-caption path.

## Is recording real or stubbed?

Real capture, real upload, real server-side storage -- with one caveat and
one contradiction worth flagging plainly.

- **Capture is real, on web.** `src/services/audioRecorder.ts` wraps the
  browser's actual `MediaRecorder` API (`:97`), negotiating a supported
  codec from a fixed candidate list (`:23-28`, `:62-72`) and encoding at
  24 kbps (`:16`) so a full 30-second clip lands near 90KB, comfortably
  under the server's 512KB ceiling (`src/services/audioRecorder.ts:11-15`).
  There is no mock/fake recorder branch; a supported browser genuinely
  records the microphone.
- **Native has no capture path.** `isRecordingSupported()` checks for
  `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` and a global `MediaRecorder`
  (`src/services/audioRecorder.ts:55-59`), both web-only APIs. On a native
  build, `supported` is always false and `/record` can only ever show the
  "not available" message this tile happens to also show (for a different
  reason, a headless capture browser). Voice notes are effectively a
  web-only path today.
- **Upload requires the live HTTP backend.** `uploadAudio()` throws
  immediately if `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_MODE` is not `"http"` or the API base URL
  is unset (`src/services/audioUpload.ts:66-68`) -- there is no mock-mode
  audio path at all, unlike `dataClient`'s mock/http split for everything
  else.
- **No transcription.** The handler's own doc comment is explicit: "No
  transcription happens on this path. The voice response is audio, and it
  stays audio" (`backend/lambda/handlers/audio-upload.ts:20-21`). `POST
  /transcribe` exists as a separate, untouched seam.
- **The 30-second cap is enforced twice, and correctly not trusted from the
  client alone.** The countdown in the UI IS the client-side cap (auto-stop
  at zero, `app/record.tsx:112-124`), and `uploadAudio()` also checks
  `durationMs` before sending (`src/services/audioUpload.ts:69-71`). But the
  server does not trust either: `audio-upload.ts` measures the decoded byte
  length itself and clamps duration server-side
  (`backend/lambda/handlers/audio-upload.ts:13-18`, `:135`), because a
  client-reported duration is not trustworthy per its own comment.
- **The contradiction to flag.** `src/lib/storyLimits.ts`'s doc comment
  says outright: "voice capture itself stays stubbed for the POC
  (realignment plan item 7 is out of scope)" (`src/lib/storyLimits.ts:6-7`).
  That is not what `app/record.tsx`, `src/services/audioRecorder.ts`, and
  `backend/lambda/handlers/audio-upload.ts` actually do -- all three
  implement real capture, real upload, and real server-side storage with
  byte/duration enforcement. Either the comment is stale (recording got
  built after it was written and nobody updated it) or "stubbed" meant
  something narrower than what it reads as. Either way, a reader trusting
  that comment over the code would materially misjudge how finished this
  feature is.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** The `next` route param (`app/record.tsx:58-60`), and
`useDraftStore.getState().imageRef` for the draft guard below.

**R6 draft guard.** Mount-only:

```
useEffect(() => {
  if (!useDraftStore.getState().imageRef) {
    router.replace(isOnboarding ? "/onboarding/canvas" : "/draw");
  }
}, []);
```

at `app/record.tsx:75-80`. This is the one draft guard in the set that
branches its bounce target: the F4 path (no `next` param, or
`next=choose-channels`) bounces to `/draw`; the F2/F3 onboarding-walls path
bounces to `/onboarding/canvas` instead, because `/record` is reused there
too.

**Writes on exit.** `audioRef`, `audioMime`, `audioDurationMs` into
`useDraftStore` on a successful upload (`app/record.tsx:187-191`); those
same fields cleared on a failed upload or a re-record
(`app/record.tsx:195`, `:131`).

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### The capture tile cannot show what this screen actually does

Because the capture tool's browser fails `isRecordingSupported()`, this
page had to establish what `/record` does entirely by reading
`src/services/audioRecorder.ts`, `src/services/audioUpload.ts`, and
`backend/lambda/handlers/audio-upload.ts` rather than by looking at a
working screenshot. That is a real gap in this capture pass: the single
most consequential fact about this screen (is recording real) is invisible
in the artifact meant to document it. A future capture run on a real
Chromium context with a fake mic device would close this.

### storyLimits.ts's "stubbed" comment is wrong, or badly out of date

Flagged in detail above. This is the kind of thing a planning session
needs surfaced plainly rather than smoothed over: a doc comment in the
codebase actively understates what shipped. Someone should either delete
the stale line or find out what "stubbed" was supposed to mean.

### Voice notes are web-only today, with no messaging that says so up front

A native user opens `/record` and sees the identical "not available" copy
this tile shows, with no distinction between "your platform can't do this"
and "this feature isn't built." `/story-select` still offers the
microphone card unconditionally on every platform (`app/story-select.tsx:65-78`),
so a native user's only signal that voice is unavailable is reaching
`/record` and reading the fallback text. Worth deciding whether the
record-card should hide or gray out on native ahead of the tap, rather than
after it.
